In a mid-Dec. 2024 matchup against the Washington Commanders , quarterback Spencer Rattler and the Saints offense had battled their way back into the game late in the fourth quarter, trailing by just one score. With nine seconds remaining and no timeouts, side judge Jim Quirk mistakenly stopped the clock following a completed pass to former Saints tight end Foster Moreau, who was ruled down at the 1-yard line. The clock stoppage gave New Orleans an opportunity to spike the ball before Rattler connected with Moreau for a touchdown on the very next play.

"It's a thing I've been doing forever," Guzzardo said after the 92-53 victory over West Georgia on Monday. "It's weird." Two eggs and some hashbrowns. That's what she eats. Doesn't matter what city or state she's in, she's still going to find a Waffle House. When asked if it was better in Athens than it is elsewhere, Guzzardo laughed out a, "No comment." For those who've never had Wafle House, first, do you live under a rock, and second, the "secret" code is simple: covered means cheese, smothered is onions and peppered is jalapenos.

Getting software to help block out a star so we can see exoplanets
stories.summary: Software optimizes a physical model of the telescope to reduce noise. While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star’s light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope’s configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets.

stories.title: Ancient Maya mercury use may have come at a severe environmental cost
stories.summary: Ancient Maya communities made extensive use of liquid mercury and a red, mercury-containing pigment called cinnabar to decorate buildings, pottery and burial sites. Unsurprisingly, as previous research has shown, this led to mercury contamination of soils and reservoirs at some Maya sites. And that pollution may have spread even farther into their territory and caused the collapse of two lake ecosystems, according to a study published in the journal Science Advances.

stories.title: Peanut allergy study finds babies should be retested. Here's what parents should know.
stories.summary: About one in 50 kids in the United States has a peanut allergy​. But a new study from Australia shows parents should consider having their kids retested. It's one of the most common hardships for parents with young kids — policing what their children eat when they are diagnosed with a peanut allergy. More than one-third of babies thought to have a peanut allergy could safely have the diagnosis removed, according to research from the Murdoch Children's Research Institute and the National Allergy Centre of Excellence, published this week in The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology.

stories.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame has begun announcing nominees for the 2027 class, and there are two former San Francisco 49ers coaches on the list. On Thursday, the Hall of Fame annonuced that five coaches are nominees, including two former San Francisco 49ers coaches: Mike Holmgren and Mike Shanahan. stories.title: DNA nanoswitches find new drug leads faster by measuring protein interactions

stories.summary: As France confronts another wave of strikes and protests, Gaëlle Martinez, National Secretary of the trade union Solidaires, presents the general strike as more than a confrontation over wages, public spending or the cost of living. Her account reveals a deeper struggle over economic dignity, the future of public services and the democratic right to collective protest. “People just want to live, not survive.” For Martinez, deteriorating schools, insufficient salaries and the dismantling of public services are not isolated policy failures. They are interconnected symptoms of political and economic priorities that, in her assessment, place fiscal restraint above social welfare. Her demand for “a new budget” that is “not based on cuts” is accompanied by a call to “tax the biggest companies, the richest companies where the profits are made.”
